newsitem.title: UK: HSBC dealing profits dip,H1 FX income grows.
newsitem.headline: HSBC dealing profits dip,H1 FX income grows.

text.p: Dealing profits at HSBC Holdings Plc fell by 11 million to 296 million pounds in the half-year to June from 307 million in the same 1996 period, HSBC figures released on Monday showed.
But HSBC's foreign exchange income at 243 million pounds was up 53 million from 190 million in the six-months to June 1996, figures accompanying full-company results showed.
HSBC profits from debt securities was unchanged at 30 million pounds while profits from interest-rate derivatives at 25 million pounds was down from 38 million in the half-year to June 1996.
Results from equities and other trading showed a two million pound loss in the six-months to June 1997 from 49 million in the same 1996 period.
HSBC said its derivatives results fell by 13 million pounds and equities and other trading results by 51 million pounds.
"The fall in equities trading was mainly due to a loss incurred on an underwriting transaction undertaken by our investment banking subsidiary in Hong Kong," HSBC said in a statement.
First-half pre-tax profits at HSBC Holdings rose 13 percent to 2.623 billion pounds, compared with analysts' expectations mostly in a range of 2.322 billion stg and 2.479 billion.
